statement: Call an integer k an admissible length when 3 <= k <= len(arr) and there exist indices a0, a1, ..., a_{k-1} such that 0 <= a0 < a1 < ... < a_{k-1} < len(arr) and, for every t with 0 <= t < k-2, arr[a_t] + arr[a_{t+1}] = arr[a_{t+2}]. The function returns a result r such that: if there is no admissible length then r = 0; otherwise r is an admissible length and every admissible length k satisfies k <= r. Thus r is the maximum admissible length, with the maximum of the empty set taken to be 0.
preconditions: 3 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr)-1, arr[i] < arr[i+1].

statement: The function returns a result r and does not fail: on every input satisfying the preconditions the Lean call produces an Ok value (no overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic).
preconditions: 3 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr)-1, arr[i] < arr[i+1].

statement: The function returns a result r and 0 <= r <= len(arr).
preconditions: 3 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr)-1, arr[i] < arr[i+1].

statement: The function returns a result r and either r = 0 or 3 <= r <= len(arr). In particular, the result is never 1 or 2.
preconditions: 3 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr)-1, arr[i] < arr[i+1].

statement: The function returns a result r and r = 0 if and only if there do not exist indices i, j, k with 0 <= i < j < k < len(arr) and arr[i] + arr[j] = arr[k].
preconditions: 3 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr)-1, arr[i] < arr[i+1].

statement: The function returns a result r and r <= 43.
preconditions: 3 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr)-1, arr[i] < arr[i+1].

statement: The function returns a result r; if r >= 3, then there exist indices a0, a1, ..., a_{r-1} such that 0 <= a0 < a1 < ... < a_{r-1} < len(arr) and, for every t with 0 <= t < r-2, arr[a_t] + arr[a_{t+1}] = arr[a_{t+2}].
preconditions: 3 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr)-1, arr[i] < arr[i+1].

statement: The function returns a result r; for every k >= 3 and every choice of indices a0, ..., a_{k-1} with 0 <= a0 < ... < a_{k-1} < len(arr), if for every t with 0 <= t < k-2 we have arr[a_t] + arr[a_{t+1}] = arr[a_{t+2}], then k <= r.
preconditions: 3 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr)-1, arr[i] < arr[i+1].

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = len(arr) if and only if for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr)-2 we have arr[i] + arr[i+1] = arr[i+2].
preconditions: 3 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr)-1, arr[i] < arr[i+1].

statement: The function returns a result r; if r >= 3, then for every k with 3 <= k <= r there exist indices a0, ..., a_{k-1} such that 0 <= a0 < ... < a_{k-1} < len(arr) and, for every t with 0 <= t < k-2, arr[a_t] + arr[a_{t+1}] = arr[a_{t+2}].
preconditions: 3 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr)-1, arr[i] < arr[i+1].
